doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Creed Taylor at Bethlehem and the studio going dark when his wife fell ill
summary: He got along with Creed Taylor from Bethlehem onward, and recalls a period when the studio closed for his wife's illness.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And you came over and there was no one there?
So during, when Bethlehem was another label that did some things for you and that’s when you met Creed Taylor.

Correct. Creed Taylor was running Bethlehem label and he was doing some interesting projects. He and I got along very well sonically. I knew exactly what he wanted, and he knew I could get it for him. Everything went swiftly from there after. Wherever he went, I went. There was a time when he used the studio exclusively.
And then there was a time when I had to shut down because my wife got ill. Then it was dark for a while.
